S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: A persistent perception that one is useless or inferior to others.
subtypes.Self-Criticism: Excessively and repeatedly blaming oneself for past minor failures or flaws.
subtypes.Reduced Self-Efficacy: Distrust in one's own ability to perform tasks or solve problems.
subtypes.Chronic Sense of Inferiority: Persistently evaluating oneself lower in comparison to others.
subtypes.Lack of Self-Assurance: Continually feeling anxious and unsure about decisions or actions.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia) is characterized by a chronically depressed or gloomy mood lasting at least two years in adults, accompanied by additional cognitive, emotional, or physical features that cause significant distress or functional impairment. The course is typically insidious and long‑standing, often beginning after a stressful life event and then persisting at a lower, steady level rather than in discrete episodes. Individuals frequently describe themselves as having "always been this way," and the disorder may coexist with major depressive episodes (double depression). It is distinguished from major depressive disorder by its chronicity, generally milder but more enduring presentation, and a more trait‑like pattern of pessimism and low self‑regard.

patient.personality: Cesar is a structured, routine‑loving man who finds quiet satisfaction in precise clerical work, solitary outdoor hobbies, and cooking traditional dishes, yet is prone to worry and self‑doubt.
patient.stressor: Roughly three years ago, mounting tension in Cesar’s marriage came to a head when his spouse accused him of being emotionally distant and overly preoccupied with work and routines, leading to a trial separation that eventually became prolonged. The separation deeply shook his self‑image; he interpreted it as confirmation that he was inadequate not just as a partner but more broadly as a person, and he quietly withdrew further into work and solitary hobbies like fishing and woodworking. Over the next two years, he kept his performance at the payroll office technically solid but stopped pursuing the supervisory role he had once eyed, telling himself he "wasn’t leadership material" and avoiding social events with coworkers and family because he felt like a failure. When his teenage daughter began canceling weekend visits and he caught himself thinking she would be "better off without a loser dad," he became frightened by how entrenched these beliefs had become and agreed to see a psychiatrist at the urging of a coworker from the food pantry where he volunteers.
patient.chief_complaint: I feel like I’m just not good enough at anything or for anyone, no matter what I do.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, sad feeling in my chest, like there’s a gray film over everything, and even when I’m doing things I used to enjoy, like cooking my mom’s recipes or going fishing, it all just feels flat and joyless, like I’m going through the motions for no real reason.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: No matter how much I sleep, I drag myself through the day at the office, and even simple things like walking up the stairs or standing at the stove to cook feel like my body weighs twice as much, so by the time I get home I just collapse in the chair instead of doing anything else.

S042.name: Low_Self_Esteem
S042.description: A persistent tendency to evaluate oneself as incompetent or worthless; chronically low self-evaluation.
S042.manifestation: I’m constantly telling myself I’m not cut out for much—at work I stick to my little payroll tasks and never speak up because I’m sure I’ll mess something up, and at home I replay the separation and think, ‘Of course she left, who would want a boring, needy guy like me?’

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: When I look ahead, all I can picture is more of the same—me alone in my small apartment, shuffling papers at the same desk until I retire, my daughter slowly drifting away—and I honestly don’t see any point in trying to change it because I just assume nothing I do will make any real difference.
